text:
alice: Heads-up — we've got a perf regression on the 8xA100 NVLink EFA cluster for the tp=2/tensor=2 config. 99th pct latency up ~18% after yesterday's kernel selector change. :thinking_face:
ben: Yikes. Which change landed? the dynamic-kernel-fallback patch?
carla: yep, that change moves short-seq inputs to the fallback (fp16->int8-kernel) earlier to avoid instability. seemed fine on single-node tests but maybe cross-node comm interacts badly.
dan: Reproduced locally with small repro: batch=4, seq=1024, kvcache warm. When we hit the fallback kernel, all-reduce stalls for ~6-8ms and kills overlap. nvlink nodes don't show as bad, infra EFA cross-node does.
alice: perf-bot posted a summary: 
perf-bot: regression detected on 2026-03-15 03:12 UTC. Metric: tokens/sec down 14% (tp2 tensor2). Trace shows increased all-reduce idle time and repeated KV cache warm restarts. Attaching top-level traces.
esther: quick ask — are we seeing KV cache invalidation across TP partitions? that would force recompute and extra comms.
carla: yes, trace shows a KV cache miss burst right after kernel swap. I suspect different kernel emits slightly different KV layout (stride/padding) so our shard alignment check marks entries invalid and we refetch.
ben: interesting. kernel selector didn't update the kv-serializer contract for fallback kernels. if the fallback changes kv byte layout we need an ABI shim or a compatibility pass.
dan: I ran `runtime-profiles --trace=comm,kv,kernel --run 12` and grabbed an async flamegraph. snippet: 
```
# sample
[comm] allreduce 0.0064s
[kernel:fast] compute 0.0018s
[kernel:fallback] compute 0.0026s
[kv:rehydrate] io 0.0059s <-- hot
```
alice: So two issues: 1) fallback kernel slower and changes KV layout causing rehydrate; 2) on EFA cross-node the all-reduce algorithm falling back to ring instead of hierarchical and can't overlap.
carla: experiments: forcing NCCL hierarchical allreduce on the job improved overlap and brought 99th down ~9%. forcing sticking to original kernel avoids KV churn and recovers another ~6%. together close to baseline.
ben: operational mitigation: add a transient kernel gating flag for dedicated clusters and v2 rollout. Longer term: update kernel selector to preserve KV layout or implement a lightweight KV layout compatibility layer.
esther: Also look at EFA queue pair sizing — oversubscription on small messages amplifies ring cost. maybe tune MPICH/NCCL params per topology.
dan: I'll put a quick PR to revert the aggressive fallback for tp2 configs and add a unit test asserting KV layout invariant across kernel variants.
alice: thanks. can someone open an incident-ish thread and tag infra (eng-infra) to check EFA qp/mtu/queue config for that cluster? also add a perf test in CI that runs cross-node tp2 with kv warm paths. :eyes:
carla: filing now. link: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-2047
perf-bot: benchmark run queued: perf/regress/1898765432 (expect ~2h).
ben: quick note: if we can't avoid layout change, consider storing per-kernel layout headers in the prefix cache to allow translation on lookup (cheap) instead of full rehydrate.
alice: good idea. assign owners in INF-2047: dan (kernel selector), carla (kv), ben (allreduce heuristics). follow-ups in eng-runtime sync.
carla: cc @perf-bot remind in 24h for status. :thumbsup:
